written.title: Five Key Things We Learned About GTA 6 From The Game Informer Cover Story
written.description: What Pure Xbox and Game Informer reported on 29 September 2026: "Five Key Things We Learned About GTA 6 From The Game Informer Cover Story", in their own words.
written.body:
This page collects what named outlets published about Grand Theft Auto VI, in their own words. This site wrote none of the sentences in quotation marks below. Each one links to the report it was taken from.

## Pure Xbox, 29 September 2026

[Five Key Things We Learned About GTA 6 From The Game Informer Cover Story](https://www.purexbox.com/news/2026/09/five-key-things-we-learned-about-gta-6-from-the-game-informer-cover-story)

The outlet's own summary:

> Just to raise your hype levels even further

> Author Profile Reply Comments 3 1 RiverGenie 1 hour ago features over 170 animal species So who wants BBQ freshly scraped off my front bumper ... um I mean sourced from ethical sustainable farm stock 🦩🍗 0 2 somnambulance 1 hour ago That’s all well and good, but I want to know about the story at this point.

> The six primary regions in the game are Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia and Mount Kalaga National Park.

> Expect manatees, flamingos, pelicans, alligators, feral cats and armadillos along the way.

## Game Informer, 2 October 2026

[The Coolest Details From Our Grand Theft Auto VI Cover Story | The Game Informer Show](https://gameinformer.com/video-podcast/2026/10/02/the-coolest-details-from-our-grand-theft-auto-vi-cover-story-the-game-0)

The outlet's own summary:

> Alex, Marcus, Charles, and Kyle sit down to discuss the most recent cover story Grand Theft Auto VI, and what Rockstar is doing with its open world systems in the new one. - Game Informer

> Marcus, Alex, Charles, and Kyle discuss how Leonida compares to Florida, the game's updated weather system and how it may compare to Red Dead Redemption 2, and speculate on what may happen to players who prey on endangered species.

Every report above is on the site's fixed source list. A report is not a confirmation: the mark on each linked entry says who said it.
